_meta.purpose: Held-out evaluation set for the 3-way intent classifier (INCIDENT | CASE_QUESTION | FOLLOW_UP).
_meta.not_used_for_training: None of these 30 questions appear in resources/intent_examples.json (the training file). They were written after the training set was frozen and were never embedded into the classifier's training matrix.
_meta.synthetic_warning: All 30 examples are hand-written, synthetic test data and have NOT been reviewed by the team member who owns the incident data. The 10 CASE_QUESTION and 10 FOLLOW_UP items are fully synthetic, so any accuracy reported on those two classes is SYNTHETIC AND INDICATIVE ONLY - it is not real-world performance.
_meta.notes: The 10 INCIDENT items use new wording that is not copied from the team file data/raw/incident_examples.json, but they are still hand-written synthetic text; treat their score the same way.

languages.hi: 10 Hindi (Devanagari) questions - synthetic, unreviewed by a native speaker
languages.mr: 10 Marathi (Devanagari) questions - synthetic, unreviewed by a native speaker
languages.hinglish: 10 Hinglish (Roman script) questions - synthetic, unreviewed by a native speaker

_meta.new_language_warning: The 30 language rows added for the multilingual encoder are SYNTHETIC and have NOT been reviewed by a native speaker of Hindi, Marathi or Hinglish. Accuracy on hi / mr / hinglish is indicative only and is not real-world performance. They are evaluation-only: none of them is used for training.
_meta.evaluation_only_note: resources/intent_test_examples.json is never used for training; training data stays in resources/intent_examples.json.
